title: Entitlement bundling experiment: fixed license + modular support add-ons and security-Q playbook
creator: Ava Patel
description: Run a 6-week pricing and contract automation experiment for Private/VPC and on‑prem customers that combines a simple fixed annual license with optional modular add-ons (support tiers, SOC/KMS/airgap options, and accelerated upgrade windows). Deliverables: 1) a recommended pricing matrix for license + add-ons targeted at mid-market and enterprise buyers, 2) a contract Q&A playbook and templated answers for common security questionnaires (SIG, CAIQ, customer RFP snippets), 3) a lightweight negotiation script and procurement checklist for sales/SEs, and 4) implementation guidance for billing + entitlement enforcement in the console. Goal is to increase deal velocity and reduce legal/security review time while preserving margin.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing matrix with recommended list prices and suggested discount bands for mid-market and enterprise (published)
Security-questionnaire playbook covering top 20 requests with templated responses and owners (published)
Sales negotiation script and procurement checklist validated in at least two active deals
Billing+entitlement implementation ticket created for engineering with clear enforcement rules and telemetry requirements
Experimental measurement plan defined and first baseline metrics collected
plan: Week 0: Align stakeholders (Legal, Security, Sales, Finance, Revenue Ops, Engineering). Collect top customer security asks and recent RFIs.
Week 1: Draft 3 pricing variants (Conservative, Balanced, Premium) with add-on components and discount guidance.
Week 2: Build security-Q playbook: map customers' top 20 questions to one-page templated responses, and assign reviewer owners.
Week 3: Run pricing sensitivity calls with 5 target accounts (sales assist) and iterate pricing bands.
Week 4: Pilot procurement checklist and negotiation script in 2 active deals; capture friction points.
Week 5: Finalize pricing matrix, playbook, and handoff to Engineering/Revenue Ops for entitlements & billing implementation.
Week 6: Measure outcomes against baseline and prepare go/no-go recommendation for wider rollout.
pricing_matrix:
Proposed components:
- Core license (annual, per-instance cap): list price $95k for ~4x GPU pool footprint equivalent; includes runtime updates and security patching, 99.9% platform uptime SLA.
- Support tiers (optional): Standard (included limited), Priority (+$18k/yr), Premium (+$45k/yr with 2-hour escalation).
- Compliance add-ons: SOC2 readiness pack (+$8k), Hosted KMS integration (+$12k), Air-gapped deployment support (+$30k setup + $10k/yr).
- Upgrade cadence choices (optional): Auto-update quarterly (included), Managed quarterly with guaranteed lead window (+$6k/yr), Locked release channel (annual major upgrades only) (+$10k/yr).
Discount guidance: mid-market typical 10-20% off list; enterprise negotiated case-by-case with floors by ARR. Rationale: keep core simple to lower procurement friction; monetize predictable support and compliance work.
security_questionnaire_flow: Owner: Security PM (Janelle Huang) with Legal reviewer (Priya Menon). Flow: 1) intake -> map to canonical playbook entry -> attach standard evidence artifacts (arch diagram, SOC statement, encryption spec) -> route to security for any deviation -> return templated response to Sales. Target SLA: initial response to common questionnaires within 5 business days; escalations (custom requirements) triaged same-day. Deliverables: consolidated answers doc, artifact bundle (arch-diagram.pdf, KMS-integration.md, audit-log-sample.csv).
